title: Signal summarization and mute policy notes
content:
Context:
Quick working notes from recent noisy-alert incidents across inference-hosting fleets. Goal is to capture lightweight experiments, temporary mitigations, and a draft approach for summarizing signals before paging humans. Want a low-effort stackable approach we can iterate on during on-call shifts.

High-level problem statements:
1) Pager noise from correlated downstream errors. Multiple alerts fire (HTTP 5xx spikes, per-route latency, cache-miss ratio) for the same root cause — operators get paged repeatedly.
2) Missing metrics intermittently cause SLO burn alerts; often due to exporter crashes or scrape auth timeouts. Current alerts alert on absolute gaps without context.
3) SLO burn alerts escalate too quickly for transient blips; we need hysteresis and contextual severity escalation.

Observed patterns & quick hypotheses:
- Many noisy clusters are caused by single node-level kube-proxy DNS flaps — manifests as: scrape errors for multiple services + elevated latencies for a subset of pods. Hypothesis: correlate exporter scrape_failures with node DNS logs and suppress duplicates.
- Missing metrics often align with cron job GC spikes that saturate egress and cause exporters to timeout for ~30–90s.
- SLO burn often triggers when synthetic requests hit overloaded GPUs during autoscaling events. The SLO burn alert lacks signal enrichment (which model, which instance type, and recent rollout tags).

Immediate mitigation experiments (low-friction):
A) Signal summarization lambda (prototype): ingest alerts for a 60s window, group by resource tag (node/pod/service), and emit a single summary alert with aggregated facets (count, top-3 metrics, most frequent alert types). Replace original alerts with suppressed copies via Datadog/PagerDuty dedupe.
  - Success criteria: reduce pages by >40% on test clusters for a week.
  - Implementation notes: use existing event-stream (Kafka topic: telemetry.alerts.v2). Add a policy that if summary emitted, individual alerts get temporary mute with correlation_id.

B) Missing-metric grace period + health-check rule:
  - For metric gaps, instead of firing on first sample miss, run a 3-sample lookahead (configurable per-metric class). If a metric is part of critical SLO, continue to escalate; otherwise, convert to a non-paging 'metric-gap' event.
  - Add an exporter-health synthetic check: a lightweight probe that scrapes the exporter endpoint from a different node agent to detect network/instance-local exporter crashes.

C) SLO burn escalation policy draft:
  - Stage 0: Informational (30s window, non-paging) when burn >1% of budget but <5% and no associated 5xx spike.
  - Stage 1: Priority page when burn >5% OR burn >2% with matching infrastructure error spike (5xx/queue_depth).
  - Stage 2: PagerDuty P1 when burn >15% OR burn is increasing >5% in last 5m.
  - Tagging: attach model-id, deployment-tag, region, instance_type to SLO events.

Runbook sketches (for on-call):
- Missing metrics / 'metric-gap' event:
  1) Check alert summary: which metric, scrape target, last successfully received timestamp.
 2) Check exporter process on target host (k8s: kubectl -n $ns get pods -o wide and describe pod; ssh if node-level).
 3) Check node-level scrape logs (prometheus/collector logs) for HTTP 500/timeout and for auth/403.
 4) If exporter died, restart pod and watch for metrics returning (expect < 2m).
 5) If network timeout, check recent network policies and host egress metrics; escalate to infra if >30% of nodes reporting.
 6) If issue persists >15m, create JIRA INC with tag observability/missing-metrics and assign to eng-sre.

- SLO burn alert (quick response):
  1) Pull SLO dashboard and look at top contributing endpoints and models (use SLO breakdown panel).
  2) Check rollout history for the service (recent deploys in last 60m). If deployment found, quarantine rollout via canary rollback or route traffic to previous model variant.
  3) If no rollout, check infra signals: GPU queue depth, pod restart counts, and per-instance CPU steal.
  4) If root cause is capacity-related, enable emergency scale-up and activate lower-tier fallback model routing if configured.
  5) Apply temporary quiet period for repeated pages for same incident (create PD incident with 'quiet window' field) and add incident note.

Signal correlation heuristics to try (notes):
- Correlate using three axes: resource (node/pod/service), symptom (5xx/latency/scrape_fail), and causal-tag (deployment tag, recent cron jobs).
- Use sliding window co-occurrence scoring: P(alert B | alert A) over last 90 days for the cluster to find stable associations.
- For high-cardinality tags (model-id), fall back to top-N only and attach counts.

Suppression & mute policy draft (temporary rules):
- Auto-mute duplicate alerts from the same resource for 10m if a summary alert exists.
- Auto-suppress downstream latent alerts that are strictly caused by upstream 504s (heuristic: same trace_id or same client_ip buckets).
- Never auto-suppress: alerts with explicit data-loss indicators, or anything that hits SLO-critical buckets.

Instrumentation and engineering fixes to prioritize:
1) Add exporter-level 'last-sample' gauge for critical exporters so we catch sample age in dashboards.
2) Tag metrics with deployment-tag and model-hash to make SLO attribution easier.
3) Harden exporter restarts: add liveness probe jitter and non-thundering restart backoff.
4) Small change to alert definition: move from absolute rate to relative percentile (90th vs 95th) when distribution is heavy-tailed.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How aggressive should summarization be for multi-tenant clusters? (risk: hiding per-customer impacts) -> action: test on staging multi-tenant cluster first.
- What retention window for co-occurrence scoring yields stable associations? 30d vs 90d? -> run offline analysis (JIRA: OBS-549).
- Policy: when to auto-mute vs annotate? Need PD policy addition for auto-muted incidents (legal/security audit concern).

Action items (short list):
- [ ] Prototype summarizer lambda hooked to telemetry.alerts.v2 (owner: Diego) — target staging rollout 2025-01-10.
- [ ] Add exporter last-sample gauge for 3 critical exporters (owner: Aisha) — PR linked in linked_artifacts.
- [ ] Implement 3-sample lookahead grace for metric gaps (owner: Jordan) — config toggles per-metric class.
- [ ] Draft PD quiet-window policy and legal review (owner: Priya)

Notes to self (on-call tips):
- When paging for SLO burn, always check for recent model/weights rollouts; most production SLO regressions we've seen are rollout-related.
- If seeing widespread missing metrics + high network egress on nodes -> consider cron/backup job correlation before chasing exporter PRs.

Retrospective checklist when incident closes:
- Record the summarizer correlation_id used for suppression (if used).
- Capture which alerts were suppressed and whether suppression hid useful signals.
- Time-to-first-meaningful-action and number-of-pagers metrics.
- If pages reduced by <25% during experiment, revert summarizer and iterate with longer windows.

End of notes.
